newsitem.title: CANADA: Norcen to sell part of Superior Propane Inc stake. [CORRECTED 20:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Norcen to sell part of Superior Propane Inc stake. [CORRECTED 20:25 GMT]

text.p: Norcen Energy Resources Ltd said on Thursday it would sell 40 percent of its interest in Superior Propane Inc by offering trust units of Superior Propane Income Fund for proceeds of C$252 million.
(Corrects to make clear Norcen is selling an interest in the operating company not the income fund.)

Norcen, which set up the fund last year with the assets of its Superior retail and wholesale propane business, said it would sell the 18.3 million trust units in a secondary offering expected to close on September 5.
Units will be sold for C$13.80 on an instalment basis to a group of underwriters, the company said.
Under the deal, the first instalment of C$6.90 will be payable upon closing and the second instalment of the same amount a year later.
Norcen said proceeds from the sale would be used to pay down debt and finance part of its 1997 capital spending.

"With Norcen's acquisition of assets in Guatemala, and a capital spending program that is expected to top C$700 million in 1997, we have several exciting oil and gas investment opportunities," Norcen Chief Executive Grant Billing said in a statement.
"Additionally, Superior Propane Inc's operating performance has been strong since the inception of the fund," Billing said.
Fund units were originally offered last September at C$10.95 each, with Norcen retaining 50 percent interest in Superior Propane Inc.

The company said on Thursday it would retain class B common shares and subordinated notes of Superior Propane Inc amounting to just over 10 percent interest. It would also continue to act as manager of the business.
The deal was the second major secondary offering announced this week in Canada's energy industry.

Oil services firm Canadian Fracmaster Ltd said late Tuesday that Chairman Alfred Balm would sell his 67.5 percent interest in that company. Balm's is a controlling stake valued at about C$550 million. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
